today.question_title: Process String with Special Operations II
hints_cache: This is a 'Reverse Simulation' problem. Since the final string is too large to store, you need to track how the string's length grows during a forward pass and then trace the index k backward to the start.

Perform a forward pass through the string s to store the length of the 'result' after every single operation. If the length ever exceeds k, you can actually stop there, as subsequent operations won't affect the character at index k unless they reverse the string.

Now, start from the end of your operations and work backward. If the current operation is a '#', the string was doubled; you can use the modulo operator to map your current index k back to its original position in the first half.

If the current operation is a '%', the string was reversed. To find what character is now at index k, you need to calculate which index it occupied before the flip by subtracting k from the total length at that moment.

Continue this backward traversal, adjusting k as you go. When you encounter a lowercase letter and your current k matches the current length minus one, you've found the character! If you finish and k is still out of bounds, return the dot.
